topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) deployment
transcript:
Header: 2026-06-25 16:00 ET | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Amy Chen (Redwood AE); Marcus Li (Redwood SE); Raj Patel (CTO, Vitality); Sara Gomez (Head of ML, Vitality); Michael O'Neill (Security Lead, Vitality)
Link references: Model catalog deck (shared), compatibility-matrix.xlsx (shared), benchmark spreadsheet (shared)

00:00 Amy Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, I see we have Raj, Sara, Michael, great to meet you all. quick agenda: walkthrough the model catalog, talk benchmarks, and then cover deployment compatibility and security.
00:22 Raj Patel: thanks amy, excited — we're trying to evaluate open models for our patient summarization pipeline, priority is sub-200ms p50 for single-turn summary and cost under $0.002 per request.
00:36 Marcus Li: ok good — we'll show model choices, the redwood performance profiles, and a compatibility matrix so you can see which models support fp16, int8, and our optimized kernels.
01:00 Sara Gomez: two quick things up front: 1) we use 512 token average inputs, sometimes up to 1k for long notes; 2) we're curious how quantization affects quality for med/clinical text.
01:18 Marcus Li: that's helpful — our catalog flags models that have been validated on clinical-like corpora and we include delta-quality metrics when running int8 or GPTQ style quantizations. quality regressions are shown per prompt set.
01:40 Michael O'Neill: security: do you have SOC2? and KMS integration? plus audit logs for inference requests? we need to map that for our compliance team.
01:58 Amy Chen: yes SOC2 Type II in place, we integrate with customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and we can surface audit logs through the console or S3 export. we'll share our compliance pack after the call.
02:15 Raj Patel: happy to see that. on infra choices, what's the recommended path: hosted or dedicated? we have sensitive PHI, so leaning private or dedicated.
02:33 Marcus Li: for PHI the typical patterns are: Hosted if you can accept Redwood-hosted and data controls, Dedicated reserved capacity if you want isolation+predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need full network isolation and customer-managed KMS. Our private deployment supports VPC peering and HSM/KMS.
03:02 Sara Gomez: can you show the compatibility matrix? which models in the catalog support low-memory int8 and batched KV caching so we can reduce per-token cost?
03:20 Marcus Li: sure sharing screen now — (note: transcript of shared screen) on the left is our model catalog table: model family, size, recommended sequence length, fp16 support, int8/gptq availability, verified perf profile, benchmark p50/p95 for 512 tokens on A100 and on T4. column for inference pattern: streaming vs non-streaming, and a column for supported runtimes.
04:05 Marcus Li: for your 512 token workloads our recommended starts are: Llama3-8B (fp16, GPTQ available), Mistral-v1-7B (fp16, limited gptq), and RedWood-2-small (our tuned variant, fp16 + optimized kernels). you'll see tradeoffs: Llama3 gives slightly better quality on hallucination metrics but costs more per token in our bench due to kernel mismatch on older GPUs.
05:10 Sara Gomez: hmm can you quantify the cost difference? we need a delta per 1k tokens.
05:25 Marcus Li: yes — in the benchmark spreadsheet: on A100 80GB Llama3-8B p50 is ~90ms and cost estimate $0.0018 per 1k tokens; Mistral-v1-7B is ~60ms and ~$0.0012; our RedWood-2-small optimized path is ~50ms and ~$0.0010 — those are ballpark for the configs we ran. we'll attach the raw csv.
06:00 Raj Patel: those numbers are helpful. how much of that improvement comes from batching or KV cache? our usage is fairly single-turn but we'd like batching when possible.
06:18 Marcus Li: good q — for single-turn p50 it's mostly model size and kernel selection; batching helps throughput and lowers unit cost but adds latency. KV cache helps when you have multi-turn chat; for summarization single-turn you'll get marginal KV benefit. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching thresholds and cache policies per route.
06:45 Michael O'Neill: about quantization — does Redwood run quantized kernels inside the same runtime, or is that a separate path and does it affect fallbacks?
07:00 Marcus Li: it's the same runtime but different execution path. we support quantized kernels (int8/GPTQ) on supported models; we also maintain compatibility flags so fallback policies can route to an fp16 variant if quality thresholds fail. those fallback routes are configurable per route.
07:35 Sara Gomez: any examples of quality delta for int8 on clinical prompts?
07:45 Marcus Li: yes in the benchmark sheet we include a delta-quality column per prompt set — e.g., on our clinical prompt set GPTQ on Llama3-8B showed ~2% drop in exact-match style metrics but often indistinguishable in human evals; for our RedWood-2-small tuned variant we saw <1% delta.
08:10 Amy Chen: i'll highlight that in the compatibility matrix — which models have validated quantization and which we recommend for production.
08:26 Raj Patel: deployment question: we want to run inference inside our VPC — is there support for sidecar or do you deploy within our subnet?
08:38 Marcus Li: Private deployment supports customer-managed control plane and worker nodes in your VPC; we do an operator that sits in your cluster or we can run a managed appliance in your private subnet. networking diagrams and a short install runbook will be included in the docs we share.
09:05 Michael O'Neill: perfect. encryption at rest and in transit? KMS for keys?
09:12 Amy Chen: yes TLS for in-transit, KMS for keys, HSM options are available for Private with enterprise add-on.
09:20 Raj Patel: ok security box checked for now — can you run a 1-2 day pilot so we can see latency on our infra?
09:30 Amy Chen: absolutely — typical pilot is 1 week with a small reserved pool; Marcus will run benchmarks and we can run your sample traces.
09:38 Marcus Li: i'll need a sample of production traces (anonymized) and a contact for infra to spin up test machines — raj can you confirm?
09:46 Raj Patel: yes I'll have infra reach out, i'll send a contact.
10:00 (brief crosstalk about calendar invites)
10:20 Marcus Li: back to catalog — another useful artifact is our model compatibility matrix which lists engine flags: supports_fp16, supports_int8, supports_kv_cache, max_sequence_len, verified_inference_kernels, recommended_gpu. for example, Mistral-v1-7B flagged as 'recommended_gpu: t4 for cost, a100 for latency'.
10:55 Sara Gomez: are there specific kernel or compile flags required for our on-prem cards? we run some older Ampere-ish boxes.
11:10 Marcus Li: our compilation layer chooses kernels based on architecture; if you have older Ampere we mark that in the matrix. there are also fallbacks which may slightly increase latency; we surface that in the perf profile.
11:35 Raj Patel: what about throughput scaling — how does Redwood autoscale for spikes?
11:46 Amy Chen: Dedicated has predictable reserved pools and burst policies; Private you can configure autoscaling with your operator and hybrid policies. we can show suggested autoscale configs based on your qps patterns.
12:05 Michael O'Neill: audit logs granularity? we need to map request id back to user id and include redaction support for PHI fields.
12:20 Marcus Li: log export includes request id, model, timestamp, duration, and metadata tags — we can also enable request body redaction and token-level sampling for logs. we'll include the log schema.
12:40 Sara Gomez: one more — model updates and rollouts — how do you prevent regressions when upgrading models?
12:52 Amy Chen: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic rollback on metrics regressions tied to prompt evals. you can pin a route to a specific model version.
13:10 Raj Patel: ok good — last thing: what's the SLA and pricing model for Dedicated vs Hosted?
13:20 Amy Chen: Hosted is usage-based (tokens + embeddings) and Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits; pricing sheet will have example tiers and cost math. we'll tailor for your projected qps.
13:40 Marcus Li: also calling out Redwood Optimize — it will suggest quant profiles, batching targets, and cost-savings per route based on your traffic. it integrates with the catalog so suggestions are model-aware.
14:05 Sara Gomez: can we get a sample Optimize recommendation for our summarization route?
14:12 Marcus Li: yes that's part of the pilot deliverable — we'll run Optimize on your sample traces and return suggested batch size, quant profile, and estimated savings.
14:30 Amy Chen: wrap-up — agreed next steps: we'll send pricing+matrix, Marcus will upload benchmark csv and inference trace, and schedule pilot kick-off. any other blockers?
14:45 Raj Patel: none from me, thanks.
14:50 Michael O'Neill: please include SOC2 docs and a network diagram.
14:55 Amy Chen: will do, thanks everyone.
15:00 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions on model names (Llama3 sometimes typed llama-3), and some overlapping talk removed for brevity.
